Declare the expected set of observational units

Source: R/expected.R
cf_expected.Rd

Builds a data frame with one row for every combination of the supplied vectors (a full cross-join), for use as the expected argument to apply_criteria(). This lets attrition be denominated against the units that should exist (e.g. every participant who was invited) rather than only the rows actually present in data – so a participant who never appears in the raw data is still counted as failing the first step that requires non-missing data, instead of being silently absent from the denominator.

Usage

cf_expected(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

Arguments

...

Named vectors of values, one per grouping variable, e.g. participant_id = 1:50, visit = c("baseline", "3mo", "6mo"). At least one named argument is required.

stringsAsFactors

Passed to expand.grid(); default FALSE.

Value

A tibble with one row per expected combination and one column per named argument in ....

See also

Other pipeline: apply_criteria(), cf_hierarchy(), continue_criteria()

Examples

cf_expected(participant_id = 1:3, visit = c("baseline", "3mo"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   participant_id visit   
#>            <int> <chr>   
#> 1              1 baseline
#> 2              2 baseline
#> 3              3 baseline
#> 4              1 3mo     
#> 5              2 3mo     
#> 6              3 3mo
